info.name: Execute a SPARQL query via GET

params.name: default-graph-uri
params.description: IRI of a graph to include in the default graph (repeatable)

params.name: named-graph-uri
params.description: IRI of a graph to include as a named graph (repeatable)

items.docs:
Executes a SPARQL query passed as the `query` URL parameter. The
query string MUST be percent-encoded. Optional `default-graph-uri`
and `named-graph-uri` parameters may be repeated to specify the
RDF dataset against which the query is evaluated.

info.name: Execute a SPARQL query via POST

items.docs:
Executes a SPARQL query via POST. Two encodings are defined by the
SPARQL 1.1 Protocol:

* `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` — the body carries the same
  parameters as the GET variant (`query`, `default-graph-uri`,
  `named-graph-uri`).
* `application/sparql-query` — the body IS the SPARQL query string,
  in UTF-8, and `default-graph-uri` / `named-graph-uri` may still
  appear in the URL query string.

Executes a SPARQL update. Two encodings are defined by the SPARQL 1.1
Protocol:

* `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` — the body carries the
  `update`, `using-graph-uri`, and `using-named-graph-uri`
  parameters.
* `application/sparql-update` — the body IS the SPARQL update
  string, in UTF-8.

Many implementations expose update on a distinct path (e.g.
`/sparql/update`) or require authentication; this is
implementation-defined.
